titulo: Will you do me a favour?
intro: Asking for a favour with tact, giving a reason, and accepting or declining politely.
p.favor.consejo: You say «hacer un favor» if you help and «pedir un favor» if you need help.
p.pedir.consejo: «Pedir» is to request something; «preguntar» is to ask a question. And e → i: «pido».
p.importar.consejo: «¿Te importa…?» asks if it bothers: to agree you answer «no», and «sí, me importa» is a refusal.
p.prestar.consejo: You «prestas» when you give something for a while, and you «pides prestado» when you receive it.
p.dejar.consejo: «¿Me dejas tu coche?» works like «¿me prestas tu coche?». It also means «permitir».
p.devolver.consejo: It changes o → ue: «devuelvo», «devuelves». It is written with v but sounds like b.
p.regar.consejo: It changes e → ie: «riego», «riegas», «riega». It is used for plants and the garden.
p.maleta.consejo: It is feminine: «la maleta». «Hacer la maleta» is to pack what you take on a trip.
p.llaves.consejo: It is the plural of «la llave». The ll sounds like a y: YA-bes.
p.es que.consejo: It goes first to give a reason or an excuse: «Es que tengo prisa».
p.claro que sí.consejo: It is a kind, sure «yes». You can also say just «claro» or «por supuesto».
p.de acuerdo.consejo: It accepts a plan or a request. It is like «vale», but a little more formal.
p.necesito que.consejo: After «necesito que» the verb goes in the subjunctive: «necesito que me ayudes».
p.me encantaría.consejo: It is conditional and used before «pero» to decline politely: «me encantaría, pero…».
b1.titulo: From an order to a favour
b1.texto:
There are many ways to ask for something. The longer and softer the sentence, the more **polite** it sounds:

- **Pásame** la sal. (direct order)
- **¿Me pasas** la sal?
- **¿Puedes** pasarme la sal?
- **¿Podrías** pasarme la sal?
- **¿Te importaría** pasarme la sal?

To ask for a favour: **¿Me haces un favor?**, **Tengo que pedirte un favor** or **Necesito que me ayudes**. You can give a reason with **es que**: *¿Me dejas tu coche? Es que el mío está en el taller.*

To accept: **claro que sí**, **de acuerdo**. To decline tactfully: **me encantaría, pero no puedo**. **No pienso hacerlo** is a very harsh no.
b2.f0.texto: Raúl, I have to ask you a favour.
b2.f2.texto: Would you mind watering my plants this weekend?
b2.f3.texto: Of course, leave me the keys and don't worry.
b2.f4.texto: Will you also lend me your big suitcase?
b2.f5.texto: The thing is, I lent it to my brother.
b2.f6.texto: And when does he give it back to you?
b2.f7.texto: He gives it back to me on Monday afternoon.
b2.f8.texto: All right, then I'll ask you for it on Monday.
b4.texto:
Spanish softens a request by changing the verb:

- **Present**: *¿Me prestas tu maleta?* With friends and family.
- **Poder in the present**: *¿Puedes prestarme tu maleta?*
- **Poder in the conditional**: *¿Podrías prestarme tu maleta?* The conditional (**-ía**) sounds less certain, and that is why it is more polite.
- **Importar**: *¿Te importaría prestarme tu maleta?* It asks whether it bothers the other person: it is the kindest form.

After **necesito que** and **quiero que**, the verb goes in the **subjunctive**: *necesito que me ayudes*.

To decline tactfully: say thank you, say **me encantaría, pero…** and give the reason with **es que**.
b4.e0.texto: Could you lend me your suitcase?
b4.e1.texto: Would you mind closing the door?
b4.e2.texto: I need you to help me.
b5.titulo: The stairs to the third floor
b5.f0.texto: The staircase of the old building smells of wood and lemon soap.
b5.f1.texto: A yellow light falls on the worn steps.
b5.f2.texto: Behind the door of the third floor a radio plays very softly.
b5.f3.texto: Someone drags a suitcase along the landing with a dull noise.
b5.f4.texto: Then a bunch of keys jingles on the doormat at the entrance.
b5.f5.texto: The plants on the balcony tilt their tired leaves towards the light.
b5.f6.texto: The brass watering can gleams next to the window like a small moon.
b5.f7.texto: The fresh water falls slowly on the dry earth and smells of distant rain.
b5.f8.texto: A new leaf opens among the others, shy and bright.
b5.f9.texto: From the hallway, the neighbour smiles with relief and closes the door.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is a direct order: fine with close friends, but not the most polite.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is a question and sounds better, but it is still very direct.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Yes! The conditional and «importar» make it the softest.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That's it! The conditional makes the request softer.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Importar» takes the third person: «te importa», not «tú importas».
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is subjunctive, and it is not needed here: an infinitive follows.
b8.traduccion: I have to ask you a favour
b9.o0.refuerzo: «No pienso…» is a very harsh no. Avoid it with friends.
b9.o1: Me encantaría, pero es que lo necesito.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! You show goodwill, give a reason and sound kind.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is correct, but curt. Add a reason or an apology.
b9.pregunta: You cannot lend your car. Which answer is kindest?
b10.frase: Necesito que me ____ con la maleta.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It is the ordinary present. Here you need the subjunctive.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not go with «que». You need a conjugated verb.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Can you lend me your car?» (use dejar)
b12.o0: Porque se la dejó a su hermano.
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it! He says it with «es que» to give the reason.
b12.o1.refuerzo: He has not lost it: his brother has it until Monday.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Raúl does want to help. The problem is that he does not have it.
b12.pregunta: Why can Raúl not lend his suitcase?
p.pedirte.consejo: The pronoun «te» attaches to the infinitive «pedir», and the stress stays on «DIR».
p.claro.consejo: As a reply it means “of course”. As an adjective it also means “clear”.
p.dime.consejo: It is the command «di» + «me». «Decir» has a short command: «di», not «dice».
p.importaría.consejo: It is the conditional of «importar». The accent on the «í» keeps «ri-a» in two syllables.
p.regarme.consejo: «Regar» + «me»: the pronoun joins the infinitive. It means “for me”, to do me the favour.
p.fin.consejo: It is masculine: «el fin». «Fin de semana» is the weekend, and it has no accent.
p.déjame.consejo: «Deja» + «me» takes an accent so the stress stays on «DE». Written without it, it would sound different.
p.prestas.consejo: It is the «tú» form of «prestar». A question like «¿me prestas…?» asks a friend to lend you something.
p.dejé.consejo: Past tense of «dejar». The accent on the «é» shows the stress, so it differs from «deje».
p.devuelve.consejo: Present of «devolver» with o → ue. The v sounds like b: de-BWEL-be.
p.prestarme.consejo: The pronoun «me» joins the infinitive «prestar». The stress stays on «TAR».
p.ayudes.consejo: Subjunctive of «ayudar», needed after «necesito que». The «-ar» verbs use e: «ayuda» → «ayudes».
p.escalones.consejo: Plural of «el escalón». The singular has an accent on the «ó»; the plural loses it.
p.gastados.consejo: Participle of «gastar» used as an adjective, so it agrees: «escalones gastados».
p.bajita.consejo: «Bajita» is a diminutive of «baja». The ending «-ita» makes it softer and more affectionate.
p.arrastra.consejo: The «rr» in the middle is a strong rolled r. The «a» before it is separate: a-RRAS-tra.
p.rellano.consejo: The «ll» sounds like a y, and the first «r» is strong: rre-YA-no. In some places it is called «descansillo».
p.manojo.consejo: The «j» sounds like a strong h. You can say «un manojo de llaves» or «de flores».
p.tintinea.consejo: It imitates the sound itself: «tin-tin». The «e-a» are two separate vowels: tin-ti-NE-a.
p.felpudo.consejo: It is the mat where you wipe your shoes. It is masculine: «el felpudo».
p.inclinan.consejo: Third person plural of «inclinar»: «ellos inclinan». Plants «se inclinan» towards the light.
p.regadero.consejo: It comes from «regar»: the thing you «riegas» with. It begins with a strong «rr» sound.
p.latón.consejo: It is masculine and ends in a stressed «ón»: «el latón». The accent shows the stress on the last syllable.
p.luna.consejo: It is feminine: «la luna». The stress is on «LU». «Luna llena» is the full moon.
p.seca.consejo: Feminine of «seco». Here it agrees with «la tierra»: «tierra seca». The «c» before a is a k.
p.otras.consejo: Feminine plural of «otro». «Entre las otras» means “among the others”, here other leaves.
p.tímida.consejo: Feminine of «tímido». All words stressed on the third-to-last syllable carry an accent: «tí-mi-da».
p.pasarme.consejo: The pronoun «me» joins the infinitive «pasar». At the table you say «¿me pasas la sal?».
p.dejó.consejo: Past tense of «dejar» for él or ella. The accent on the «ó» tells it apart from «dejo».
